searchText: so, if 'verbatim', that would translate to bytecode `0xe834`, and exchange 5th and 10th stack items (1-based), correct? This is why I think we need punctuation for verbatim and effective values. EXCHANGE really leaned into execution efficiency at the expense of casual readability. ahh so you mean there would be two ways to write it? EXCHANGE !0x34 for verbatim and EXCHANGE 5,10 for effective. But SWAPxx is already off by 1 for DUPxxx, so it's a hot mess any way we code it. wait, why does `0xe834` exchange 5 and 10? I thought it would exchange `4` and `5`? ahh, reading EIP > the n + 1‘th stack item is swapped with the n + m + 1‘th stack item. Not the way things are named now, but SWAP[2] (swap 2n'd with 1st, currently SWAP @ 0x90), DUP[2] (dup the second item, current DUP2 @ 0x81)) and EXCHANGE[2,3] (0xe800) and then SWAP[!0x01], DUP[!0x02], EXCHANGE[!0x00] would be literal encodings. I would just use the `[xxx]` for specifying verbatim immediates (without `!`) So `DUP 2` `SWAP 2` `EXCHANGE 5, 10` would be `DUP[01]` `SWAP[00]` `EXCHANGE[00]` yes I could live with that Ok, require fully zero-ed out nybbles, so `JUMP[0003]` would be the literal `JUMP :label` if label resolved to 3? and JUMPV -- YOLO? well, you don't have to write the verbatim encoding usually for example, in geas right now, I support the syntax `jump @label` and it expands into `pushX @label; jump` right, it's a fallback for stunts like `RJUMPI[FFFD]` to clear all non-zero stack items so in geas, all instructions can have an immediate syntax-wise, but it's only supported for jump and push in EOF, more instructions can have an immediate, and for jumps one would usually write `rjumpv @label` but it's a good idea to support the verbatim syntax as a separate concept Yes, that is the best case. But crazy coders and decompilers will still have a fallback. `self: RJUMPI @self` is much more readable anyway btw I don't have the time right now to implement EOF in geas but it's good to have the syntax ironed out ahead of time. I worked on it a bit around devcon, and finished some important precursor changes, but now I'm busy with other things on the topic of syntax, what might be a good way to handle sections? there are two approaches one is delimiting them explicitly, for example with ``` #section XXX { op op } ``` this would kind of go with the data section notation that is still pending https://github.com/fjl/geas/issues/7 another way would be just declaring the start of a section, ending the current one: ``` #section XXX op op #section YYY op op ``` I guess it depends on the container model, does EOF support nesting a section in the middle of another one? probably not No nesting sections, but also no jumps crossing section boundaries. code section within another code section - no. But a container in the container section is an EOF container so contains moar sections nested, but that is probably not interresting to the assembler And sections needs at least two metadata items, input stack and output stack. Max stack height/extra stack should be computed by the assembler. We could presume 0 in the absence of the metadata, but it needs to be settable. Yes yes sections are rather functions Yeah, so I've been thinking how to represent that. The geas language is kind of sigil-based, so there has to be a prefix for section names. & is still free, so it'll be that most likely this kind of confusion is why verbatim is probably not the best option! rjumpi[fffd]

excerpts.author: pdobacz
excerpts.content: so, if 'verbatim', that would translate to bytecode `0xe834`, and exchange 5th and 10th stack items (1-based), correct?

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: This is why I think we need punctuation for verbatim and effective values.  EXCHANGE really leaned into execution efficiency at the expense of casual readability.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: ahh so you mean there would be two ways to write it?

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: EXCHANGE !0x34 for verbatim and EXCHANGE 5,10 for effective.  But SWAPxx is already off by 1 for DUPxxx, so it's a hot mess any way we code it.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: wait, why does `0xe834` exchange 5 and 10? I thought it would exchange `4` and `5`?

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: ahh, reading EIP

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: > the n + 1‘th stack item is swapped with the n + m + 1‘th stack item.

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: Not the way things are named now, but SWAP[2] (swap 2n'd with 1st, currently SWAP @ 0x90), DUP[2] (dup the second item, current DUP2 @ 0x81)) and EXCHANGE[2,3] (0xe800)

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: and then SWAP[!0x01], DUP[!0x02], EXCHANGE[!0x00] would be literal encodings.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: I would just use the `[xxx]` for specifying verbatim immediates (without `!`)

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: So `DUP 2` `SWAP 2` `EXCHANGE 5, 10` would be `DUP[01]`  `SWAP[00]` `EXCHANGE[00]`

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: yes

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: I could live with that

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: Ok, require fully zero-ed out nybbles, so `JUMP[0003]` would be the literal `JUMP :label` if label resolved to 3?

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: and JUMPV -- YOLO?

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: well, you don't have to write the verbatim encoding usually

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: for example, in geas right now, I support the syntax `jump @label` and it expands into `pushX @label; jump`

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: right, it's a fallback for stunts like `RJUMPI[FFFD]` to clear all non-zero stack items

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: so in geas, all instructions can have an immediate syntax-wise, but it's only supported for jump and push

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: in EOF, more instructions can have an immediate, and for jumps one would usually write `rjumpv @label`

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: but it's a good idea to support the verbatim syntax as a separate concept

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: Yes, that is the best case.  But crazy coders and decompilers will still have a fallback.  `self: RJUMPI @self` is much more readable anyway

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: one is delimiting them explicitly, for example with

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content:
```
#section XXX {
   op
   op
}
```

this would kind of go with the data section notation that is still pending https://github.com/fjl/geas/issues/7

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content:
another way would be just declaring the start of a section, ending the current one:

```
#section XXX
  op
  op

#section YYY
  op
  op
```

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: I guess it depends on the container model, does EOF support nesting a section in the middle of another one?

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: probably not

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: No nesting sections, but also no jumps crossing section boundaries.

excerpts.content: code section within another code section - no. But a container in the container section is an EOF container so contains moar sections nested, but that is probably not interresting to the assembler
